prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: [adversarial] Rowspan taller than its rows (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "All three steps share on" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Step" · longest unbreakable unit 35px · widest one-line content 35px
  col 2: header "Owner" · longest unbreakable unit 48px · widest one-line content 48px
  col 3: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable unit 76px · widest one-line content 1797px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 438px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 438px wide (column widths sum to at most 437px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 438px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Show who owns each step and the note shared by all three steps.","tasks":["Find the owner of a named step.","Compare ownership across the three steps.","Read the shared note in connection with the sequence Plan, Build, Ship."],"relations":["Plan belongs to Ana, Build to Ben, and Ship to Cai.","The Notes cell spans all three steps; its text applies to the group rather than to Plan alone."],"roles":["The header row labels the step, owner, and shared-note columns.","Each of the three body rows identifies one step and its owner.","The tall Notes cell is a single group-level annotation."],"keep_whole":["Step names, owner names, and column headers.","Words and identifiers within the shared note."],"may_wrap":["The shared note can wrap naturally between words; its full text is not visible in the supplied overview."],"same_scale":["The three step rows and their owner cells should remain easy to scan as a comparable set.","The three column headers share the same structural role."],"h_vs_v":"The short step and owner labels need little width, while the long shared note benefits strongly from extra width. A narrower note increases the height of the merged cell and the space distributed across its three rows; wider label columns can make row lookup more spacious but make the note longer vertically."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d1r0A, d1r0B, d1r0C.
Measured facts:
d1r0A: column widths [56, 69, 312] px · table 438×213 px · row heights [36, 59, 59, 59] · column headers on >1 line: 0/3 · tallest cell 7 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 438 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r0B: column widths [75, 85, 277] px · table 438×236 px · row heights [36, 66, 66, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 0/3 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 438 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r0C: column widths [100, 110, 227] px · table 438×283 px · row heights [36, 82, 82, 82] · column headers on >1 line: 0/3 · tallest cell 10 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 438 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). This is your first look at real renders: propose at least one improved or alternative design (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or test an important idea you have not tried). "done" is not allowed yet. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
